hwe_bench.problem_statement: When Rocket Chip is elaborated with Sv57 virtual memory (five page-table levels) and hypervisor support enabled together, the PTW (page-table walker) can build cached page-table-entry addresses by extracting an index from a shifted address fragment that is narrower than the requested slice width. The observed behavior is that hardware elaboration fails with an out-of-range bit-index error in the PTW instead of generating the design. The expected behavior is that the Sv57-plus-hypervisor configuration should elaborate successfully, and PTW cached PTE address generation should not index past the available bits. The affected function is the PTW cached page-table-entry address generation used during hypervisor page-table walks. The trigger condition is enabling both Sv57 (`PgLevels = 5`) and hypervisor support in the same Rocket Chip configuration.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Form the 56-bit address by zero-extending the complete 35-bit VPN fragment with nine high zeros and twelve low page-offset zeros.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: Sv57 plus hypervisor configuration built a page-table address from a fragment narrower than the slice assumed by the implementation.
